name: polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome overview
title: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) pathway: oligomenorrhoea or hyperandrogenism is worked by first excluding the lecture's seven mimics, from one slide per limb of the triad, then applying the diagnostic triad of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction and exclusion with no ultrasound required; each limb and the associated insulin resistance gets its history and exam, tests, and treatment by the symptom of distress, with metabolic and endometrial risk management

nodes.title: Oligomenorrhoea and/or hyperandrogenism
lines: EXCLUDE the mimics first, then apply the diagnostic TRIAD

nodes.title: EXCLUDE first: the lecture's 7 mimics
lines: pregnancy · hyperprolactinaemia · exogenous testosterone · tumour producing testosterone · congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) · hyperthyroidism · early menarche or menopause

nodes.title: PMOS: polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
lines: renamed in 2026 from polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): the follicles are ARRESTED ANTRAL FOLLICLES, not cysts · the ovary is a TARGET, not the source
over 170 million women, up to 20% of reproductive age · multisystem, NO single cause identified

nodes.title: Which limb of the triad does it mimic?
lines: the deck gives one mimics slide per limb

nodes.title: Diagnostic TRIAD: ALL THREE needed · NO ultrasound required
lines: 1 · hyperandrogenism: clinical exam OR labs (↑ testosterone) · 2 · ovulatory dysfunction: oligomenorrhoea OR cystic ovaries on ultrasound · 3 · exclusion of other disorders
~no gold-standard test · insulin resistance is ASSOCIATED, not a 4th criterion
~older schemes: Rotterdam 2003, 2 of 3 with ultrasound its own criterion · Androgen Excess Society 2008, 3 of 3

nodes.title: Mimics of HYPERANDROGENISM
lines: 3 on the deck's slide

nodes.title: Mimics of OLIGOMENORRHOEA
lines: 4 on the deck's slide

nodes.title: Hyperandrogenism
lines: hirsutism · acne · alopecia
met by clinical exam OR labs

nodes.title: Ovulatory dysfunction
lines: oligomenorrhoea OR cystic ovaries on ultrasound

nodes.title: Insulin resistance + metabolic risk
lines: associated, not a criterion
the ovaries carry insulin + IGF (insulin-like growth factor) receptors

nodes.title: Exogenous testosterone
lines: taking it, or contact with a PARTNER's topical testosterone
→ a thorough medication + social history

nodes.title: Tumour making testosterone
lines: adrenal (incl. adrenal Cushing's) or ovarian
RAPID onset of hyperandrogenism on history
~PMOS: GRADUAL onset

nodes.title: Early menarche or menopause
lines: → a thorough menstrual history: no test

nodes.title: Hyperprolactinaemia
lines: GALACTORRHOEA (milky breast discharge)
~PMOS: NO galactorrhoea

nodes.title: Hyperthyroidism
lines: thyrotoxic symptoms: palpitations, hair fall, tremor, weight loss

nodes.title: History
lines: hirsutism, acne: location + timing of onset
alopecia: presence + timing · family history of hirsutism

nodes.title: Before calling hair abnormal
lines: weigh rate of onset · ethnicity · parental appearance

nodes.title: Exam: TERMINAL, male-pattern hair
lines: sides of face, chin, anterior chest, upper arms · acne · frontal alopecia
~lower-arm + upper-lip hair can be normal

nodes.title: Modified Ferriman-Gallwey score
lines: 9 sites, each graded 1–4
ignores ethnicity + hair removal

nodes.title: Hirsutism is defined by DISTRESS
lines: unwanted hair enough to distress her, not a score

nodes.title: Menstrual history
lines: age at menarche
how often: initially · later teens · after age 20
oral contraceptive use · family history: irregular menses, infertility

nodes.title: Just stopped the pill, now irregular?
lines: the pill did NOT cause it: it masked oligomenorrhoea she already had

nodes.title: Take a GENTLE weight history
lines: cycles irregular after significant weight gain?

nodes.title: NOT all with PMOS are overweight
Personal history
lines: diabetes or prediabetes · obstructive sleep apnoea · metabolic liver disease

nodes.title: Family history
lines: diabetes mellitus, incl. gestational diabetes

nodes.title: Central (visceral) adiposity
lines: visual assessment can suffice · waist ÷ hip > 0.85 in women

nodes.title: Skin
lines: ACANTHOSIS nigricans: back of neck, axilla · skin tags

nodes.title: Tumour: ↑↑↑ testosterone
lines: → imaging

nodes.title: CAH: MILD 21-hydroxylase deficiency
lines: ↑ 17-alpha-hydroxyprogesterone

nodes.title: Pregnancy: ↑ serum beta-hCG
lines: beta-human chorionic gonadotropin

nodes.title: Prolactin ↑
lines: normal < 20 nmol/L

nodes.title: Thyroid: ↓ TSH, ↑ free T4
lines: thyroid-stimulating hormone · thyroxine

nodes.title: Total testosterone
lines: the only androgen used here (not DHEAS = dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, nor androstenedione)
female normal < 2 nmol/L · male range from ~8

nodes.title: ~2.1–2.5 nmol/L: slightly raised
lines: fits PMOS

nodes.title: A NORMAL level does NOT exclude PMOS
lines: may be normal or only slightly raised · the exam alone meets this limb

nodes.title: Pelvic ultrasound: NOT required
lines: peripheral follicles = arrested antral follicles, not cysts
an ALTERNATIVE route into this limb

nodes.title: Cystic ovaries are not specific
lines: seen early after menarche and in some normally cycling women

nodes.title: MONITOR for
lines: diabetes mellitus (DM) · hypertension (HTN) · cardiovascular disease

nodes.title: Testosterone ~10 nmol/L is NOT PMOS
lines: inside the male range: points to a TUMOUR

nodes.title: Positive beta-hCG: NOT PMOS
lines: the whole plan forks on it

nodes.title: Hirsutism
lines: surface: epilation, shaving, sugaring, waxing, laser
oral: antiandrogens (spironolactone, cyproterone) · birth control pill (BCP)
topical: EFLORNITHINE (Vaniqa)
~counsel: surface hair removal won't make it worse · response lags, may be partial

nodes.title: Alopecia
lines: MINOXIDIL 5% (Rogaine) · antiandrogens · BCP · hair transplant

nodes.title: NOT topical testosterone
lines: (Androgel): the one wrong treatment

nodes.title: Irregular cycles
lines: BCP or cyclical progesterone · weight loss, exercise

nodes.title: Protect the endometrium
lines: endometrial cancer is more common: induce WITHDRAWAL BLEEDS ≥ 4× a year (oral contraceptive or cyclical progesterone)
ultrasound surveillance for endometrial hypertrophy

nodes.title: Subfertility
lines: lifestyle · induce ovulation with AROMATASE INHIBITORS · metformin (arguably) for early miscarriage

nodes.title: Ovarian stroma surgery
lines: partial resection, drilling, thermal ablation: RARE now

nodes.title: She CAN conceive spontaneously
lines: harder, but certainly possible
→ effective contraception if pregnancy is not wanted yet

nodes.title: Lifestyle
lines: high fibre, low fat diet · planned exercise ~half an hour daily · MODEST weight loss

nodes.title: NO body shaming
lines: collaborate with compassion: meet patients where they are

nodes.title: Manage metabolic risk
lines: 150 min planned vigorous exercise weekly · high fibre, low fat · moderate weight loss

nodes.title: Consider BARIATRIC surgery
lines: ~quite effective for restoring menstrual cycles and fertility
lowers metabolic syndrome risks

panels.title: The lecturer's summary: high yield
items: history: oligomenorrhoea · hirsutism · NO galactorrhoea · GRADUAL onset
exam: hirsutism · acanthosis · acne · alopecia · ↑ body mass index (BMI), visceral adiposity
risk monitoring: endometrial cancer · DM, HTN, lipids

panels.title: Myths to dispel
items: TRUE: subfertility + early miscarriage · metabolic syndrome correlates (type 2 DM, HTN, high lipids) · endometrial cancer · mood disorders
FALSE: cannot lose weight · always hungry · organic or vegan diet helps · cannot conceive

panels.title: More common with PMOS
items: gestational diabetes · frontal alopecia · central adiposity · endometrial carcinoma

panels.title: Contributing mechanisms
items: luteinizing hormone (LH) ↑, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) ↓: drives theca androgens
peripheral fat converts adrenal androgens to testosterone
